title: Etale closed-support bounds for the transported pro-etale exceptional functor
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow T$. Suppose $(W,T)$ satisfies the ordinary etale open-complement condition at $A$ with an integer $c\geq0$ [def-exc-open-complement-bound]. Write $i_e^!$ for the ordinary etale right adjoint to closed direct image, and let $Ri^!=
u_Z^*i_e^!R
u_{T,*}$ be the transported functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], with $
u_S:S_{\mathrm{proet}}	o S_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For integers $r\leq s$ the following two assertions hold separately.

1. If $B\in D_c^{[r,s]}(T,A)$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals], there is a bounded constructible ordinary etale complex $B_e$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:
u_T^*B_e\cong B$, with $\mathcal H^t(B_e)=0$ for $t
otin[r,s]$. For any such witness there is a natural identification
$$Ri^!B\cong
u_Z^*i_e^!B_e,$$
and
$$Ri^!B\in D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}(Z,A).$$
No finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed on $B$ in this assertion.
2. If $B\in D^b_c(T,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], then every bounded constructible etale witness $B_e$ for $B$ has etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$, meaning $\mathcal H^t(B_e\otimes_A^LM_e)=0$ for every degree-zero etale $A$-module sheaf $M_e$ and $t
otin[r,s]$. The object $Ri^!B$ is bounded constructible and has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s+c+1]$, tested against every degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaf on $Z$, whether or not it comes from the etale site.

proof.text: The coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ is finite and commutative. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] to $T$ and $A$. For clause 1 it supplies $B_e\in D_c^b(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:\nu_T^*B_e\xrightarrow{\sim}B$; its reflection of each cohomological interval puts $B_e$ in $[r,s]$. The same equivalence supplies a bounded constructible witness for the input of clause 2. No Tor hypothesis is used to obtain either witness.

proof.text:
For any bounded constructible witness $(B_e,\alpha)$, $B_e$ is bounded below, so [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives the invertible unit $\eta_{B_e}:B_e	o R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*B_e$. Put $F=
u_Z^*i_e^!$. By the finite defining formula in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], the composite
$$F(B_e)\xrightarrow{F(\eta_{B_e})}F(R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*B_e)\xrightarrow{F(R
u_{T,*}\alpha)}Ri^!B$$
is an isomorphism; its inverse is the claimed identification. Naturality of the unit and functoriality give naturality in morphisms of witnesses: for $ eta:B_e	o B'_e$ and $h:B	o B'$ satisfying $h\alpha=\alpha'
u_T^* eta$, the displayed composites intertwine $F( eta)$ and $Ri^!(h)$.

source.place: Tag 099V, lemma-relative-comparison (2); apply the unit to the finite transported formula.

proof.text: For clause 1, the two clauses of [def-exc-open-complement-bound] are precisely the vanishing and constructibility hypotheses of [lem-exc-closed-amplitude], with $a=r$, $b=s$ and the given $c\geq0$. That lemma gives $C_e=i_e^!B_e\in D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] on $Z$: $\nu_Z^*C_e$ is bounded constructible and lies in that same interval. The isomorphism of Step 2 gives the asserted membership for $Ri^!B$. This proves clause 1 without imposing finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: Step 2: closed-support cohomological computation; expanded using the ordinary etale amplitude lemma and Tag 09AL.

proof.text: For clause 2 choose any bounded constructible etale witness $B_e$ and invert its witness isomorphism to write $B\cong\nu_T^*B_e$. Apply [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii), with interval $[r,s]$. Its assumptions hold: $B$ is bounded constructible, its pro-etale Tor interval is given, $B_e$ is bounded below, and $\ell$ is invertible on the $k$-scheme $T$ since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. It follows that $B_e$ has etale Tor amplitude $[r,s]$, with the vanishing test for every degree-zero etale module sheaf $M_e$. The argument applies to every witness, not only the one chosen in Step 1.

source.place: Clause (ii), reflection of the Tor interval.

proof.text: Apply [prop-exc-closed-tor] to $B_e$, using Step 4 and the two ordinary etale hypotheses supplied by [def-exc-open-complement-bound]. Its coefficient ring is exactly $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $j$ is the given quasi-compact complementary open, and $c\geq0$. Thus $C_e=i_e^!B_e$ is bounded constructible with etale Tor amplitude $[r,s+c+1]$. Apply [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i) on $Z$ to $C_e$ and this interval (it is nonempty since $r\leq s$ and $c\geq0$). It gives bounded constructibility and the same pro-etale Tor interval for $\nu_Z^*C_e$. This predicate tests every degree-zero pro-etale module sheaf, with no etale-origin restriction. Tensor the Step 2 isomorphism with each such sheaf and take cohomology; the resulting cohomology isomorphisms give the identical vanishing for $Ri^!B$.
